correctness.rationale: The published CDF is a positive power of a smooth function B_theta(x) normalized by B_theta(1), with B_theta prime at one strictly positive. Taylor expansion gives survival linear in 1-x with a positive coefficient and a finite positive endpoint density; their ratio is asymptotic to 1/(1-x). A second-order expansion gives h prime asymptotic to 1/(1-x)^2. The packaged checker independently verifies the endpoint ratios and a representative interior-decline example.

value.rationale: Hazard-shape flexibility is a central advertised feature of the TEA model for reliability data. The endpoint theorem removes one entire claimed global hazard class and explains why finite-range plots can be misleading near a hard truncation boundary. The correction also applies unchanged to the later progressive-censoring analysis, so it materially affects reliability interpretation across both papers.
